title: The Debt of the Free Port
premise: Mirabel Sterling, a freelance interpreter who handles the delegations, cargo manifests, and confessions that governments prefer unattributed, is hired for a peace summit in the free port of Vhalen. Midway through negotiations, Flight 447—a charter carrying both delegations' financial auditors—vanishes from every radar log, passenger list, and memory while still airborne, leaving only Mirabel's contemporaneous translation notes as proof it existed. Hunted by the port's syndicate, the summit's host, and her own handler, she discovers the flight was erased to bury evidence that the peace itself was financed by stolen reparations funds. To survive, Mirabel must trade her one protected secret—the identity of the broker who taught her the erasure trade—for justice no court will ever record, ending with her testimony delivered off the books and her old life permanently deleted.
about_author: Rosalind Dravenmoor spent a decade working contract interpretation jobs in border cities before turning to fiction, drawing on the bureaucratic shadows where official records simply stop existing. She writes under a pen name because, as she puts it, some debts are easier to pay anonymously.

chapters.title: The Unattributed Hand
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. In Vhalen's fog-bound free port, Mirabel takes a last-minute contract interpreting for a fragile peace delegation, establishing her rules: no names kept, no copies made, no allegiances. She notices the summit's financial annex has been redrafted overnight without explanation. Emotional beat: wary professionalism masking a lifetime of learned invisibility.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. At the opening session, she interprets a concession she knows is false, catching a delegate's micro-flinch that suggests he's reading her translation rather than hearing it. Her old handler, Casimir Voss, appears uninvited at the hotel bar, reminding her of an open favor. Emotional beat: the first crack in her belief that neutrality protects her.

chapters.title: Flight 447
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The delegations' joint auditors depart on charter Flight 447 to retrieve sealed ledgers; Mirabel interprets their pre-flight briefing and logs every name in her working notes. Over the radio relay, the pilot confirms cruising altitude—then static. Emotional beat: ordinary routine curdling into dread as the transmission dies mid-sentence.

chapters.title: Nothing Was Ever Scheduled
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. By morning, Flight 447 exists nowhere: no manifest, no fuel purchase, no departure slot. Airport staff genuinely remember nothing. Only Mirabel's handwritten notes preserve the flight's reality—and someone begins asking, very politely, whether she keeps notes. Emotional beat: gaslit vertigo; her invisibility weaponized against her.

chapters.title: The Ledger That Isn't
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Cross-checking the summit's financial annex against her memory of the original draft, she finds the reparations funding clause rewritten to launder a vanished sum. The numbers only make sense if Flight 447's auditors were meant to find them. Emotional beat: cold clarity replacing fear—she was hired to be the record they forgot to erase.

chapters.title: Casimir's Favor
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Voss offers protection in exchange for her notes, hinting he helped build the erasure trade years ago and knows its mechanics. He names the technique—a 'scrubbing'—but not its current operator. Emotional beat: temptation and disgust; accepting help means admitting she never left his world.

chapters.title: Interpreter, Witness
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. A delegate's aide, Sefa Idrizi, privately reveals she also remembers the flight—her sister was aboard—and begs Mirabel to corroborate her. Two witnesses make them dangerous. That night Mirabel's hotel room is searched with surgical politeness. Emotional beat: solidarity kindling into shared purpose, and shared risk.

chapters.title: The Port Remembers Nothing
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Mirabel works the port's gray economy—a customs clerk, a tug pilot, a records-house archivist—piecing together fuel tonnage and crew rosters that prove 447 flew. Each source dries up within hours of contact. Emotional beat: mounting horror as the scrubbing operates faster than she can dig.

chapters.title: What the Broker Sold
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Following Voss's half-hints, she identifies the style of the erasure: it matches the work of 'the Cartographer,' the broker who trained her years ago and whose identity she has guarded ever since—the secret worth killing for. Emotional beat: betrayal of self; her own discretion may be the murder weapon's blueprint.

chapters.title: A Delegation of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The summit resumes as if nothing happened; the auditors' chairs stand empty and unremarked. Mirabel deliberately mistranslates a key clause to stall the settlement, buying time but painting a target. Emotional beat: quiet defiance—the first time she uses her skill as a weapon rather than a shield.

chapters.title: Sefa's Proof
chapters.summary: POV Sefa Idrizi. Sefa retrieves her sister's boarding photo from a family cloud backup the scrubbers missed, plus a voicemail sent mid-flight describing 'men meeting the plane.' She and Mirabel compare notes and realize the flight landed somewhere, once. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into evidence; hope with a body count attached.

chapters.title: The Hangar at Kilometer Nine
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Tracing fuel logistics, they locate a decommissioned hangar outside the port zone containing a burned airframe stripped of its registration. Among the ash: a auditor's case with a partial ledger page bearing the reparations account number. Emotional beat: grim vindication shadowed by the smell of what happened here.

chapters.title: Host Country Hospitality
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The summit's host, Minister-Regent Aldous Kreyn, invites Mirabel to a private tea where he offers her a lucrative permanent post—and mentions her childhood village with unsettling accuracy. The message is unmistakable. Emotional beat: velvet menace; power showing her exactly how small she is.

chapters.title: Notes on Fire
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Her working notes are stolen from the delegation's secure room—an inside job. With her primary evidence gone, Sefa's backup becomes the last copy of the truth, making Sefa the next target. Emotional beat: loss and guilt; her rules of anonymity have endangered the one person who trusted her.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Map
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Deciphering the burned ledger page's accounting codes, Mirabel recognizes the Cartographer's signature routing scheme—meaning the broker personally designed this erasure. Voss confirms it, then warns her: the Cartographer will come to close the loop, and she is the loop. Emotional beat: hunted certainty; the past arriving on schedule.

chapters.title: Trade Terms
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The Cartographer contacts her directly: her silence and Sefa's backup in exchange for her life and a clean exit. Mirabel counteroffers—her secret (the broker's true identity) for the full ledger and the landing-site witness list. Negotiation becomes confession. Emotional beat: terrifying agency; she finally prices the thing she swore never to sell.

chapters.title: Kreyn's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Mirabel confronts Kreyn with the partial ledger, forcing him to admit the peace was bought with stolen reparations money and the auditors' deaths were the balancing entry. He argues the settlement saves thousands of lives; two dozen dead auditors were the discount. Emotional beat: moral vertigo—justice and peace priced against each other.

chapters.title: The Exchange at Low Tide
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. At a derelict pier, the trade happens: Mirabel surrenders the Cartographer's identity to Voss's people while the Cartographer's courier delivers the ledger—but the exchange is ambushed by Kreyn's men tying off loose ends. Voss takes a bullet shielding her. Emotional beat: chaos and sacrifice; every debt coming due at once.

chapters.title: Everything Translated, Nothing Recorded
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Wounded and cornered in the records house, Mirabel broadcasts the full ledger and flight reconstruction over the port's shipping channels, ship-to-shore frequencies, and every interpreter's relay she can reach—making the truth too widely heard to scrub. Emotional beat: cathartic release; the invisible woman becoming a signal no one can jam.

chapters.title: The Fall of the Free Port's Peace
chapters.summary: POV Sefa Idrizi. The broadcast detonates the summit; delegates walk out, Kreyn's patron states withdraw support, and international investigators arrive to a scandal that cannot be redacted fast enough. Sefa publicly names her sister among the dead, forcing the flight back into existence. Emotional beat: bitter triumph—justice achieved, peace destroyed, both earned.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Testifying off the record to investigators, Mirabel trades her final knowledge for immunity and Sefa's protection, watching the Cartographer's network dismantled piece by piece. Voss survives, changed; Kreyn faces a tribunal that will take years. Emotional beat: exhausted accounting; the price paid tallied honestly at last.

chapters.title: The Debt of the Free Port
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Months later, Mirabel works a minor trade conference under a new name, keeping no notes, making no copies. Sefa sends a postcard: her sister's name now carved on a real memorial. Mirabel allows herself one written sentence in her own hand—then burns it. Emotional beat: hard-won peace; survival as a debt she'll spend a lifetime repaying.
